oneTimers: Arm's $43M tax benefit included a one-time benefit: the non-GAAP tax rate was 5.6% but would have been 13.5% without it — the benefit did much of the work in turning a $64M operating profit into $107M of net income.
Arm recorded a $10M loss from equity investments in the quarter, which it strips out of its non-GAAP results: excluding it (and share-based pay), non-GAAP net income was $317M versus $107M GAAP.
otherDetail: Other items netted to zero: $29M of net interest income was offset by a $19M other non-operating loss, and equity investments lost $10M. Tax was a $43M benefit — a 67.2% effective benefit rate — including a one-time benefit (the non-GAAP tax rate would have been 13.5% without it).
pngFooterNote: Record Q2 royalties; a tax benefit lifted net income.

segments.name: License and other revenue
segments.note: Fees for licensing Arm chip designs, plus support and related services; down 15% YoY on the timing and size of high-value license agreements and contributions from backlog, though bookings were strong and ACV grew 13% YoY.

segments.name: Royalty revenue
segments.note: A cut of every chip shipped with Arm technology inside; up 23% YoY to a record for a Q2 on wider use of the Armv9 architecture — now around 25% of royalty revenue, up from around 10% a year ago — and smartphone market recovery, including Apple's iPhone 16 and MediaTek's Dimensity 9400.

takeaways.text: Revenue rose 5% to $844M, above the high end of guidance ($780–830M), on record second-quarter royalty revenue. Royalty revenue grew 23% to $514M while license revenue fell 15% to $330M on the timing of high-value deals — but bookings were strong, ACV grew 13% to $1,253M, and RPO rose 10% sequentially to $2,385M. For the first half of the fiscal year, revenue was $1,783M, up 20% year over year.
takeaways.title: Revenue beat guidance on record royalties

takeaways.text: Royalty revenue grew 23% to $514M on wider use of the Armv9 architecture and smartphone market recovery. Armv9 now contributes around 25% of royalty revenue, up from around 10% a year ago, with smartphone application-processor royalties growing strongly on Apple's iPhone 16 and MediaTek's Dimensity 9400. Microsoft's Azure Cobalt 100 and Google's Axion, both Arm-based cloud chips, reached general availability in the quarter.
takeaways.title: Royalties keep climbing on Armv9

takeaways.text: GAAP net income was $107M, or $0.10 per share, versus a $0.11 loss a year ago — but operating income was just $64M, a 7.6% margin, as R&D climbed to $507M on a 21% jump in engineering headcount. A $43M tax benefit, including a one-time benefit, plus $29M of net interest income did the heavy lifting. Excluding the equity loss and share-based pay, non-GAAP net income was $317M, or $0.30 per share. Free cash flow was -$65M on working-capital timing.
takeaways.title: A tax benefit did the heavy lifting

verdict: Arm's revenue rose 5% to $844M, above the high end of guidance, on record second-quarter royalty revenue of $514M, and a $43M tax benefit lifted a thin $64M operating profit to $107M of net income.
